findings.summary: No demonstration covers the production call site, so the fix can go unwired with every test green.
findings.evidence: The criterion 2-4 tests call check_reading_acceptance and then check_named_dependencies directly with fixture arguments. The real refusal happens in read_once (reading.rs 499-530): build_reading, then ls_tree, then check_reading_acceptance, then ReadError::Refused. If the new call is never added there, or the cat_blobs text loading is wrong, all planned tests still pass while no real reading is refused. The request asks for a test that fails without the change, for the cause. Fix: Add one test at the reader level, using the fake driver as in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs or the read_for callers at reading.rs:838 and :1011. Its reader output names a path absent from the base commit. Assert the result is ReadError::Refused naming the path, and that the reader runs again with the refusal as a correction. If the test cannot reach that level, add a small seam in read_once that the test drives, and name it.
findings.location: Demonstrations, criteria 2-4; plan step 3 (wiring in read_for)

findings.summary: A name counts as existing if it is mentioned anywhere in .rs/.toml text, including comments, strings and test fixtures; the plan's own fixtures will make the motivating name count.
findings.evidence: A Grep for check_code_health|context_engineer|context-engineer in crates/ finds nothing today. Criterion 3 case (c) puts `check_code_health` into reading.rs tests as a fixture. After landing, a whole-word match finds it, so a later reading that says it already exists passes. Doc comments that describe planned functions count the same way. That is the plan's own reason for excluding .md (Decision 4). Fix: Match definitions only: fn, struct, enum, trait, const, static, type, mod, macro_rules! and similar, with the name as a whole word. Or strip comments and string literals before matching, or leave #[cfg(test)] modules out of the searched text. In tests, build fixture names from pieces so the source never holds them whole. Record the choice in D146.
findings.location: Decision 4 / plan step 3 (contains_word over the .rs/.toml corpus)

findings.summary: The acceptance check runs in read_once, not read_for.
findings.evidence: reading.rs:313 read_for calls read_once twice; check_reading_acceptance is called at reading.rs:520 inside read_once (fn at 372). Fix: Name read_once as the call site in step 3 and Decision 1.

findings.summary: The UPPER_SNAKE and CamelCase patterns as worded could match all-capital emphasis words or brand names.
findings.evidence: The plan extracts 'snake_case, UPPER_SNAKE, CamelCase ... of at least 5 characters' without requiring an underscore for upper-case names or an internal case change for CamelCase. Words like NEVER, ALWAYS or HTTPS would become candidates, and are refused when the code does not contain them. Fix: Require at least one underscore for all-capital names, and a lowercase-to-uppercase change for CamelCase. Add a guard test showing a plain all-caps word is not checked.

findings.summary: A job id named only in the request is not checked unless the reading repeats it, which narrows the stated cause.
findings.evidence: The request's cause says a job id named in the request or notes is taken to mean its work landed. Part 3 fires only when the reading's own text names the id. A reading can rely on a request-cited job's role or work without repeating the id. Fix: Either apply Part 3 to every referenced job from the request (referenced_jobs already holds them), with the id in out_of_scope as the one-token exemption, or record this narrowing in D146 next to the role-words narrowing.

summary: The plan fixes the right place, the reading-acceptance step in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. The code it names exists: check_boundary_and_repo_files, check_reading_acceptance, names_path_token, unaccounted_files, code_surveys, path_exists_in, EarlierAttempt with changed_files and reading_deliverables, Git::cat_blobs, and the ids in git's file listing. Keeping the check as a separate pure function, and judging whether earlier work landed by the files at the base commit, are sound. Two problems need revision. First, every demonstration calls the new function directly, so a producer that writes check_named_dependencies but never calls it in read_once (where readings are actually accepted) passes every planned test while nothing is refused in production. Second, the symbol check counts a name as existing if it appears anywhere in .rs/.toml text, including comments, strings and test fixtures. The plan's own test fixture `check_code_health` (I found it nowhere in crates/ today) would then make that name count as existing in later jobs. This is the same weakness the plan gives for leaving out .md. Smaller points: the call site is read_once, not read_for; the name patterns are loose; and a job id that only the request names is not checked.
